card.statement:
One can construct a category of fiber functors over $X$, and prove that $\mathsf{St}_{X}$ embeds fully faithfully in the category of fiber functors (see [9, Lemma 2.3.4]). We say that a fiber functor is representable if it belongs to the essential image of $\mathsf{St}_{X}$. Then, in the situation of Definition 2.1 the fiber functors $\mathcal{F}_{X\smallsetminus T}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{T}}}$ are representable, while in general $\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{T}}}^{\mathrm{aff}}$ and $\mathcal{F}_{\widehat{T}\smallsetminus T}$ are not.

Now let $D$ be an effective Cartier divisor in $X$ and $Z\subset D$ a closed subscheme of codimension $1$ inside $D$. Let us denote by $\widehat{D}$ a representative (in the sense of Remark 2.2) for $\mathcal{F}_{\widehat{D}}$. We would like to have a notion of formal completion ${\widehat{Z}}^{\widehat{D}}$ of $Z$ inside $\widehat{D}$. But [7, Proposition 6.3.1] shows that $\widehat{D}$ is in general an ind-scheme, so we provide details for the construction of ${\widehat{Z}}^{\widehat{D}}$.

We start by writing $\widehat{D}$ as a formal colimit of schemes $\widehat{D}=\colim D_{n}$. If $\mathcal{I}_{D}$ is the ideal sheaf defining $D$, then $D_{n}=\Spec_{X}(\mathcal{O}_{X}/\mathcal{I}^{n+1}_{D})$. Using the formalism of fiber functors, each $D_{n}$ can be also constructed as follows. Since $D$ is a closed subscheme in $X$, for every affine scheme $S=\Spec R$ there exists an ideal $I_{D,R}$ such that $\mathcal{F}_{D}(S/X)=\Spec(R/I_{D,R})$. For every natural number $n$, we then set

$\mathcal{F}_{D_{n}}(S/X)=\Spec(R/I_{D,R}^{n+1}).$

Then $Z$ is a closed subscheme of each of the $D_{n}$, so that we can construct the formal completions ${\widehat{Z}}^{D_{n}}$. For every affine $S=\Spec R$, let $I_{Z,R}$ be the ideal defining the closed subscheme $\mathcal{F}_{Z}(S/X)$ in $S$. Notice that in particular $I_{D,R}\subset I_{Z,R}$. Then the fiber functor $\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{D_{n}}}$ is defined as

$\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{D_{n}}}(S/X)=\colim_{m\in\mathbb{N}}\Spec\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(R/(I_{D,R}^{n}+I_{Z,R}^{m})}}\right).$

We set

$\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{\widehat{D}}}(S/X)=\colim_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\colim_{m\in\mathbb{N}}\Spec(R/(I_{D,R}^{n}+I_{Z,R}^{m}).$

The fiber functor $\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{D}}$ is therefore an objectwise ind-ind-scheme, so that a priori we can define various affinization of it. For example, we can first consider an affinized version of $\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{D_{n}}}$, namely

$\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{D_{n}}}^{\mathrm{aff}}(S/X)=\Spec\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\lim_{m\in\mathbb{N}}R/(I_{D,R}^{n}+I_{Z,R}^{m})}}\right)$

and use it to define

$\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{\widehat{D}}}^{\mathrm{aff},\widehat{D}}(S/X)=\colim_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{D_{n}}}^{\mathrm{aff}}(S/X)=\colim_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\Spec\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\lim_{m\in\mathbb{N}}R/(I_{D,R}^{n}+I_{Z,R}^{m})}}\right).$

Here $\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{\widehat{D}}}^{\mathrm{aff},\widehat{D}}$ has to be thought as the fiber functor encoding the ind-affine formal neighborhood of $Z$ inside the ind-scheme $\widehat{D}$. In particular, $\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{\widehat{D}}}^{\mathrm{aff},\widehat{D}}$ takes values in ind-affine schemes, and not in affine schemes.

Alternatively, we can consider the affinization of $\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{\widehat{D}}}$ defined as follows:

$\mathcal{F}_{{\widehat{Z}}^{\widehat{D}}}^{\mathrm{aff}}(S/X)=\Spec\mathopen{}\mathclose{{\left(\lim_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\lim_{m\in\mathbb{N}}R/(I_{D,R}^{n}+I_{Z,R}^{m})}}\right)$
card.label: Remark 2.2

paper.title: Two dimensional versions of the affine Grassmannian and their geometric description
paper.abstract: For a smooth affine algebraic group $G$ over an algebraically closed field, we consider several two-variables generalizations of the affine Grassmannian $G(\!(t)\!)/G[\![t]\!]$, given by quotients of the double loop group $G(\!(x)\!)(\!(y)\!)$. We prove that they are representable by ind-schemes if $G$ is solvable. Given a smooth surface $X$ and a flag of subschemes of $X$, we provide a geometric interpretation of the two-variables Grassmannians, in terms of bundles and trivialisation data defined on appropriate loci in $X$, which depend on the flag.
